# Copilot Instructions (edge-cache-lab)

## Big picture
- This repo is a mini e-commerce API focused on CDN/Varnish cache behavior; the OpenAPI contract is the source of truth for endpoints, headers, and models.
- Go API server lives in apps/api; handlers implement the generated ServerInterface from openapi/api.yaml (codegen output in apps/api/internal/api/api.gen.go).
- Cache behavior is explicit: public endpoints set Cache-Control, Surrogate-Control, ETag, X-Cache; private endpoints are no-store.
- Responses include request id + response meta (timestamp, instance, headers received) to aid cache debugging.

## Critical workflows
- OpenAPI validation + codegen:
  - make openapi-validate
  - make openapi
- API dev loop:
  - make api-init (first time), make api-install, make api-run
  - make api-test, make api-lint, make api-fmt
- Docker local stack:
  - make docker-up, make docker-logs, make docker-down

## Conventions and patterns
- Do not add routes by hand. Add/modify endpoints in openapi/api.yaml, then regenerate code.
- Do not edit apps/api/internal/api/api.gen.go; it is generated by oapi-codegen.
- Handlers live in apps/api/cmd/server/main.go and should satisfy the generated ServerInterface.
- Cacheable endpoints should call setCacheHeaders() and return X-Request-Id plus response meta.
- Non-cacheable endpoints must set Cache-Control to no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate.
- Admin update responses should include X-Purge-Tags (purge tag string like product:{id}).
- Request logging uses middleware.RequestID and a custom requestLogger (log includes request_id and latency_ms).
- Instance identity comes from INSTANCE_NAME env var or hostname.

## Integration points
- openapi/api.yaml drives server interface and types (oapi-codegen).
- Docker Compose exposes the API on port 3000 with INSTANCE_NAME set.
- Tests in apps/api/cmd/server/main_test.go validate cache headers, request id behavior, and contract responses.
